terminal_mode_configure_desc: Set up WiFi, login stuff, and more! Comes with a chatty little console~
terminal_mode_flash_desc: Give your device a shiny new brain~
terminal_mode_raw_desc: Just the console. Listen to your device chatter and boop it with commands~
terminal_erase_desc: Wipes everything, even its old settings
terminal_unsupported: Your browser can't do this one, sowwy...
terminal_update_browser: Pwease update your browser to the newest version~
terminal_use_browsers: Try one of these browsers, cutie:
terminal_connect_failed_bootloader: Couldn't get it into bootloader mode... *whimpers*
terminal_connect_failed_desc: I tried and tried, but your device wouldn't talk to me.
terminal_try_replug: Unplug it and plug it back in~
terminal_try_cable: Try a different USB cable or port.
terminal_try_driver: Make sure the serial driver is installed!
terminal_help_desc: Go through these one by one. Each one sniffs out a common problem~
terminal_help_cable_body: Lots of USB-C and micro-USB cables can only charge and can't carry data. Grab a data cable you know works (one you've moved files with before) and plug your hubby back in~
terminal_help_port_body: Plug your device straight into your computer. USB hubs, docks, and front ports can be fussy with power and signal. On a desktop, try a port on the back~
terminal_help_driver_extract: Unzip it into a folder on your computer.
terminal_help_driver_run: Open the folder and run {#code}CP210xVCPInstaller_x64.exe{/code}. Just follow along~
terminal_help_manual_intro: Driver installed but your device is still hiding?
terminal_help_manual_open: Open Device Manager (press {#key}Win{/key} + {#key}X{/key} and pick {#code}Device Manager{/code}).
terminal_help_manual_ports: Under {#code}Ports (COM & LPT){/code}, sniff out something like:
terminal_help_manual_missing: Not there? Windows can't see your device at all, so go back to the cable and port steps.
terminal_help_manual_browse: Choose {#code}Browse my computer for drivers{/code} and pick the folder you unzipped the driver into. Make sure {#code}Include subfolders{/code} is ticked!
terminal_help_manual_success: If it worked, it should now say {#code}Silicon Labs CP210x USB to UART Bridge{/code}! Yay~
terminal_help_discord_intro: Still stuck? Come to our Discord den and ask in {#code}# 💭┃support-chat{/code}! Tell us:
terminal_help_discord_device: which device you have (board model, where you got it)
terminal_help_discord_tried: what you already tried from the steps before
terminal_help_discord_errors: any error messages or console output
terminal_risk_intro: You're about to flash {#strong}experimental firmware{/strong} that's {#strong}known to be wobbly{/strong}.
terminal_risk_brick: This might turn your device into a brick, need manual rescuing, or just break it. For real.
terminal_risk_no_support: We can NOT help you with problems this firmware causes.
terminal_risk_acknowledge: I understand this is all on me
terminal_channel_recommended: This is the comfy recommended channel~ ♡
terminal_channel_danger: DON'T USE THIS UNLESS YOU REALLY KNOW WHAT YOU'RE DOING
terminal_flash_rebooting: Rebooting... (unplug and replug the power if it gets stuck)
terminal_flash_done: All done! Your device has a shiny new brain ✨
terminal_cfg_intro: Values get sent to your device over UART, and it answers in the console below. Commands without an argument just read the value; press the {#eye/} button next to a field to peek at it~
terminal_cfg_rf_desc: How your device talks to its zappy fwiends.
terminal_cfg_keepalive_desc: Gives your zappy fwiends a little poke now and then so they don't fall asleep~
terminal_cfg_estop_desc: A big button that stops everything right away.
terminal_cfg_estop_note: Psst: {#code}estop.latching{/code} and {#code}estop.active{/code} don't have their own commands; set them in the JSON config below.
terminal_cfg_wifi_desc: Network logins and what your device is called.
terminal_cfg_invalid_json_array: That's not a valid JSON array, silly~
terminal_cfg_ap_note: AP settings ({#code}ap_ssid{/code}, {#code}ap_password{/code}, {#code}ap_disabled{/code}, {#code}sta_disabled{/code}, {#code}offline_mode{/code}) don't have their own commands; use the JSON config.
terminal_cfg_backend_desc: Where your device phones home, and how it logs in.
terminal_cfg_domain_restart: Setting the domain makes your device take a quick nap and restart.
terminal_cfg_echo_desc: Your device repeats what you type, like a little parrot~
terminal_cfg_advanced_desc: For things without their own commands (captive portal, OTA, LAN, and so on), swap out the whole config.
terminal_cfg_read_json: Peek at the config as JSON
terminal_cfg_json_restart: Applying a JSON config makes your device restart.
terminal_cfg_read_raw: Peek at the config as base64
terminal_cfg_factory_reset_confirm: This forgets everything on your device: WiFi networks, backend logins, pins, all of it. It'll be like brand new.
terminal_cfg_read_failed_desc: Your device stayed quiet after {attempts} tries... *pouts*
terminal_cfg_cause_busy: Your device is busy with another command.
terminal_cfg_cause_disconnected: Your device unplugged or took a nap.
terminal_cfg_cause_unsupported: This firmware doesn't know that command yet.
hubs_subtitle: All the hubbies living in your den~
hubs_empty_desc: A hubby passes your boops along to your zappy fwiends. Add one to get started!
hub_reboot_desc: Your hubby will doze off and wake back up. Its zappy fwiends won't listen until it's back~
hub_hotspot_enable_title: Let {name} open its own Wi-Fi hotspot?
hub_hotspot_enable_desc: Your hubby opens its own little setup network. It stays on your Wi-Fi too, but anyone nearby can join the hotspot until you turn it off.
hub_hotspot_disable_desc: The setup hotspot closes. If your hubby isn't on your Wi-Fi yet, you'll need to go poke it in person to set it up again.
hub_delete_desc: You're about to say bye-bye to {#strong}{name}{/strong}... *sniffles*
hub_delete_shockers: These zappy fwiends will go too:
hub_pair_consumed: {#strong}{name}{/strong} gobbled up the code and is now paired!
hub_pair_used: That code is all used up now.
hub_copy_now: You only get to see this code once, so copy it now and give it to your clients~
hub_pair_generate_for: You're about to make a pairing code for {#strong}{name}{/strong}.
hub_pair_one_active: Each hubby only gets one code at a time, so a new one replaces the old one.
hub_token_regenerate_for: You're about to make a new token for {#strong}{name}{/strong}.
hub_token_invalidate: The old token stops working and anything using it gets disconnected.
hub_update_unstable_warning: This one might not be stable and could have some bugs crawling around.
hub_update_subtitle: Give this hubby a shiny new brain~
hub_update_rolled_back: Your device went back to its old brain
hub_update_card_desc: Pick a channel and version for your hubby~
hub_update_must_be_online: Your hubby has to be awake first!
hub_update_no_history: No updates yet for this hubby.
